title: Technical diagrams / Usage

location.series: IBM Design Language / public web guidelines
location.extent: Complete webpage content area, default interactive state

slide_intent: Make system relationships explicit so readers do not have to infer meaning from unexplained symbols.
strategic_value: Legends, consistent nodes and clear subsystem boundaries can make IBM technical communications easier to interpret.
demonstration: Document and screen examples precede clarity comparisons, product-guidance routing and an IT architecture vocabulary table.
practical_value: Choose the right diagram system, add a legend and text labels, and preserve semantic differences between node types.

content_islands.name: Examples in use
content_islands.spec: Begin with documents, printed diagrams and screen applications.

content_islands.name: Clarity comparisons
content_islands.spec: Use approved and rejected legends, labels, zoom access, nesting and node examples.

content_islands.name: Carbon boundary
content_islands.spec: Explain when to switch to product components rather than communication-diagram guidance.

content_islands.name: Subsystem vocabulary
content_islands.spec: List architecture concepts beside their notation and link to specialist resources and documentation kits.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source prioritizes clarity and correct interpretation of relationships and architectural models.
reference_purposes.Application: Examples explain legends, labels, nested fills, zoom access and specialist architecture notation.
reference_purposes.Constraint: General guidance applies outside product screens; product diagrams use Carbon guidance. Essential information must have words as well as icons, and new subsystem elements require approval.

ingredient.name: Technical diagram semantics
ingredient.role: Make the meaning of relationships and nodes explicit.
ingredient.application: Include a legend and words for essential information; offer zoom or download when a diagram cannot be displayed at 100%. Use node differences only for semantic differences.
ingredient.scope: Documentation, presentation and collateral diagrams. Product interfaces follow Carbon; architecture subsystems also retain their specialized notation.
